batches.title: Music
batches.note: The four long-form tracks. Listen with the loop toggle on: the only question that matters for music here is whether you can hear the seam when it wraps. — SIGN-OFF 2026-08-27: 4 of these are already approved and unchanged (Menu, Office ambient 1, Office ambient 2, Walkthrough) — no need to judge them again.

items.name: Menu
items.why: Plays under the badly-designed building on the main menu. Wants to be curious rather than grand — this is a game about drawing, not about saving the world.

batches.title: UI sounds
batches.note: Every click, snap and chime the player hears through the in-game computer. Play them back to back — they have to sound like one set of hardware, not thirteen downloads. — SIGN-OFF 2026-08-27: 1 of these is already approved and unchanged (Click soft) — no need to judge it again. 12 are NEW since you last listened and need a fresh verdict.

items.name: Click soft
items.why: Hover and secondary presses. The same character as the confirm click but quieter and duller, so the two read as one family.

meta.licence: Proprietary — Microsoft Windows system audio, supplied by the project owner
meta.author: Microsoft Corporation
meta.origTitle: A Microsoft Windows startup chime, **release not identified**: the file arrived as an unlabelled `w.mp3` with no title metadata. Measured: three struck bell notes, F♯3 → C♯4 → G♯4 over 0.9 s, then a 1.6 s shimmering decay. It is demonstrably neither the XP nor the Vista chime (both supplied separately here and measured differently), and matches the Windows 7 / Windows 8-era startup chime in structure. Named by measurement rather than by guess.

changedSince.applied: REPLACED with your own file (w.mp3): an unlabelled Microsoft startup chime, three struck notes F#3 -> C#4 -> G#4 and a 1.6 s tail. NOT CC0 — see CREDITS.md.

batches.title: Headline models

Judge them at the scale figure: 1.75 m, standing next to the model, with the real bounding box in metres under it.
